title: Sundown PR heuristics and refactor seedbank
content:
Purpose: capture small heuristics and tiny refactor ideas during late-day review sessions. Not a formal playbook — a seedbank I can skim when I have 20-40 minutes and want to clear small debts.

Quick heuristics (sundown run):
- Aim for 20-minute scope: either a single failing test, a small naming change, or a 1-2 line guard. If it grows, open a follow-up ticket.
- Prefer mechanical, low-risk edits: rename, extract tiny helper, clear ambiguous comment, tighten test assertions.
- When in doubt about behavior impact, add an assertion test first rather than changing production code.
- Favor explicitness over clever shortcuts in hot paths; add a TODO comment with a ticket id if you leave a micro-optimization undone.

Checklist for a quick PR pass (my personal minimal gate):
- Does the change ship a single behavior? If no, split or document with follow-up.
- Are tests added/updated for the most important axis (edge case or failure mode)? If not, quick test or mark with 'needs-test' and ticket.
- Are names clear to a reader who only sees file-level diffs? Rename if cognitive load > 2 clicks.
- Is there a new dependency or heavy refactor? Gate for a morning deeper review.
- Any operation/observability implications? Add metrics/logging note or small trace.

Refactor seeds (tiny ideas I keep reusing):
- Extract 'request validation' from route handlers into explicit package method with deterministic error shapes. Good for small PRs: move 10-20 lines + tests.
- Replace repeated optional param parsing with a lightweight Option struct and helper constructors — one test, several callsites simplified.
- Swap ad-hoc string matching for a tiny enum wrapper when there are 3+ cases. Minimal risk, big readability.
- Localize feature-flag checks to a single helper when multiple scattered ifs exist; add one integration smoke test.
- Convert duplicated retry backoff snippets to a single util with configurable policy. Add 1 test for policy behavior.

Follow-ups and tickets to create (if I don't handle now):
- FR-req-cache: investigate mismatched cache TTL observed in PR #4217 integration test. Ticket: ENG-1321. Quick steps: add repro test, snapshot timings, propose TTL alignment.
- Cleanup-legacy-protos: a pair of tiny proto adapters in the auth package; surface for a small refactor sprint. Ticket: ENG-1343.

Notes-to-self on risk signals while reviewing:
- Large diff in hot path + small test changes = red flag. If observed, revert to 'add test' first.
- Subtle contract changes to exported helpers require changelog note and a try-rollout with canary.
- Any change touching KV cache code: prefer a unit test that mocks sequence of cache hits/misses rather than only integration.

Evening quick-run script I use mentally:
1) Open PR -> scan title + description (30s).
2) Look at changed files; skip vendor/auto-generated (30s).
3) Run key tests locally for touched packages (5-10m).
4) Read through one representative file, check naming and edge handling (5m).
5) If everything looks small and safe, leave a short review with 1-2 suggestions and a thumbs up. If not, mark 'needs-work' and add clear next steps.

Examples of short review comments I leave often:
- "Nit: rename 'cfg' to 'serverCfg' — improves clarity when skimming."
- "Add a negative test for empty input case; small and catches regression."
- "Move this validation into validation.go to avoid duplicated logic later."

Unresolved questions / ideas to test later:
- Does tightening parse behavior in route X affect older clients? Add contract test or bump compatibility note.
- Could we add a lint rule to catch repeated magic strings in the storage layer? Prototype a grep-based check.

End-of-day grooming actions (if I'm the reviewer):
- Triage PRs that I flagged 'follow-up ticket' into a small backlog for the week.
- If several tiny refactors accumulate, batch them into a single low-risk cleanup cycle.
- Share two concise examples with the team for review ergonomics improvements.

Rough todos (short):
- ENG-1321: add TTL repro test (10-20m).
- ENG-1343: list adapters and plan change (30m).
- Prototype small lint for magic strings (spike, 1-2h).

Footnote: keep this file short and evolving. It's a scratchpad; prune stale seeds monthly.
